messages:
emily: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose a segmented entry-path for new models to reduce cost and catch compatibility earlier. Rough idea: three lanes: fast-smoke, kv-weighted-smoke, deep-bench. Fast-smoke = existing lite checks. KV-weighted-smoke = small-ish workload that stresses KV/caching and seqlen/attention edgecases and returns a compact 'kv-health' fingerprint. Deep-bench = full regression + quality evals.

vikram: this sounds promising. question: how do we route artifacts into lanes? on upload or after initial lite pass?

emily: route on upload: run fast-smoke immediately. If it passes, then kv-weighted-smoke runs async with higher parallelism but a sample budget. If kv-weighted fails, block deep-bench until owner ack. Also default to deep-bench override for enterprise customers.

ben: cost-wise we should ensure kv-weighted-smoke is tiny. what's the expected token/sample budget? also prefer running kv-weighted on representative checkpoints only (not every patch).

emily: agreed. proposal: kv-weighted-smoke = ~500 sequences (stratified by seqlen) total ~200k tokens. We do a 2-step sampling: deterministic golden seeds + reservoir sample from recent user traces. That should exercise KV paths without blowing cost.

ben: ok. can we express the lane config as a small declarative snippet so infra can enforce budgets?

emily: yes — sketch: ```yaml
lanes:
  fast-smoke:
    budget_tokens: 5000
    checks: [sanity, tokenizer, small-latency]
  kv-weighted-smoke:
    budget_tokens: 200000
    checks: [kv-health, seqlen-distribution, perf-regressions]
    stratify: [1-64,65-256,257-1024]
  deep-bench:
    budget_tokens: 5_000_000
    checks: [full-bench, quality-evals]
    trigger: [manual, kv-fail, scheduled]
```

sara: +1. Two gating points: (1) thresholding for kv-health needs to be interpretable (e.g. pass if relative-latency < 1.5x and token-bleu > .95 vs golden) and (2) telemetry must tag model variants so runtime can select fallback if kv-health is low.

emily: agreed on both. We should publish a small kv-health vector: {latency_ratio, kv-miss-rate, kv-tail-p90}. Keep it compact so other services can weight it.

vikram: how do we handle quantized variants? kv-behavior can differ a lot once weights are quantized/packed. Do we run kv-weighted-smoke on each quantization profile?

emily: good catch. My proposal: run kv-weighted-smoke on the canonical float checkpoint + 1 representative quant profile (the default quant config for that model family). If the operator uploads additional quant variants, they get a light check (fast-smoke) and a delta-check against canonical kv-vector. If delta > threshold, gate.

ben: rollout ops: what about canary windows and staged releases to Dedicated? we don't want a bad kv-vector landing to heavy traffic.

emily: rollout plan: canary to 1% traffic for 48h with kv telemetry stream. If kv-tail spikes or error-rate > baseline, auto rollback. We'll add a manual guard for enterprise contracts.

onboard-bot: Ticket created: #ML-ONB-4123 "Segmented entry-paths + kv-weighted smoke plan" (assignee: emily).

sara: next steps: (a) finalize pass/fail thresholds + sample sets, (b) add lane schema to intake service (YAML -> enforced budget), (c) add kv-health vector to runtime model metadata. Who owns (b)?

emily: i'll take (a) and (c). vikram volunteers for (b) — will draft the intake schema + enforcement hooks. ben will prototype sampling harness and cost sim.

vikram: i'll start a small PR for intake schema. we should also add a feature flag so we can opt models into segmented lanes during rollout.

emily: yes — feature flag + metrics dashboard. meeting to sync next Tue 10am. Thanks all :thumbsup:
